sampling_model.design: Observational long-panel sampling with two predeclared square donor/proxy partitions and deterministic treatment onset after period \(n\).
sampling_model.units: One treated unit and a fixed-dimensional vector of untreated controls observed for \(n+m\) periods.
sampling_model.treatment: The treated outcome equals \(Y_t(0)\) before onset and \(Y_t(0)+\Delta_t\) afterward; controls remain untreated.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; identification is through two valid proximal bridge systems with fixed singular-value margin.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each bridge is estimated from pre-treatment moments. The conventional procedure uses all \(n\) pre-period observations for both selection and bridge fitting, replaces the bridge Jacobian, post donor mean, bridge coefficient, and ATT in its influence scores, and uses separate pre- and post-period Bartlett estimates with \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\). The correction instead selects early, discards a logarithm-squared gap, fits late, averages post residuals, and uses Bartlett bandwidth \(h_n=\lfloor\min(|\mathcal B_n|,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For a predetermined donor/proxy partition, the proximal bridge moment identifies the synthetic-control weights and fixed-role GMM/HAC inference is asymptotically normal.
Conditioning a Gaussian linear statistic on a polyhedral selection event yields an exact truncated-normal pivot and conditional confidence interval.
Explicit Gaussian formulas characterize coverage of naive and protected intervals after selection between two nested regression models.
Even functionals are invariant under the paper's skew-symmetric perturbation construction.
Separated-block sample splitting is asymptotically valid for broad beta-mixing time-series functionals under stability conditions.
Kernel long-run covariance estimators are consistent under serial dependence and suitable bandwidth growth.
Section 5, Theorem 3 establishes asymptotic normality of the article's doubly robust GMM estimator when at least one of its two bridge models is correctly specified.
For a fixed proximal proxy structure, influence functions, semiparametric efficiency bounds, and locally efficient estimators are characterized.
Simultaneous protection over all candidate submodels guarantees post-selection coverage under arbitrary selection rules.

body.tldr: Two valid proximal synthetic-control role assignments can identify the same ATT yet produce a nonregular conventional interval when the role with smaller pre-period ridge loss is reported. The same-sample conventional interval is fully specified by fitted bridge and post-residual influence scores and separate Bartlett long-run variance estimates with bandwidth \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\). The project derives its selected-Gaussian law and exact coverage function, proves that every exact selector tie preserves every symmetric Wald level, establishes all-gap validity exactly when the two standardized ATT coordinates have equal squared correlations with the loss contrast, and signs strict miscoverage otherwise. A finite-dimensional primitive Gaussian chart realizes both regimes; its explicit asymmetric point has limiting coverage \(0.8858209104904335\) for a nominal \(90\%\) interval, and strict miscoverage persists in the chart's Euclidean relative topology. The distinct correction separates early role selection from late bridge fitting and post residual averaging; its remaining open theorem asks for uniform selector-conditional Bartlett-studentized normality over whole triangular arrays with a fixed finite root-\(n\) loss-gap envelope and singular joint covariances.

project_justification.gap: Published proximal synthetic-control theory predetermines donor and proxy roles, while general selective-inference theory does not characterize unconditional conventional symmetric-Wald coverage for a statistic that changes coordinates with the selected role.
project_justification.niche: The binary ridge selector has enough Gaussian geometry for an exact if-and-only-if coverage frontier, yet its covariance coordinates retain a substantive proximal interpretation through bridge Jacobians, donor means, and long-run residual variation.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the selected limit, the evaluable coverage map, the squared-correlation frontier and strict sign rule, a continuous finite-dimensional primitive realization map, and a separated estimator whose uniform singular-covariance mapping over bounded-gap triangular arrays is exposed as the first-class open question.

body.related_work: Shi et al. (2026) provide the writing and causal setup exemplar: excluded controls serve as supplemental proxies, fixed bridge moments identify a synthetic-control ATT, and long-panel GMM uses HAC inference. The present theorem changes the first post-linearization step by allowing two predeclared valid roles to be selected with the same observations. Lee et al. (2016) supply the Gaussian half-space conditioning technique, but their target is an exact conditional selective pivot. Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald (2015) demonstrate that explicit post-selection coverage calculations are possible for nested regression models; their selector and reported target differ from the proximal switched-coordinate functional here. Azzalini and Regoli (2012) explain the even-function symmetry behind exact tie protection, so symmetry alone is not claimed as new. Lunde (2019) supplies the separated-block beta-mixing transfer, and Andrews (1991) supplies Bartlett-HAC control; both are supporting methods for the corrected estimator. Section 5, Theorem 3 of Qiu et al. (2024) gives asymptotic normality for the article's doubly robust GMM estimator when at least one of its two bridge models is correctly specified; it is fixed-role machinery rather than a role-selection result. Cui et al. (2024) provide fixed-proxy proximal influence-function and efficiency theory. Berk et al. (2013) give universally protected simultaneous intervals, whereas the present target is the exact frontier on which the ordinary role-specific critical value already works.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The Gaussian coverage algebra and the finite-dimensional primitive covariance map have direct calculations, but the publication-level uniform joint Gaussian/HAC mapping over singular stacked covariances remains open. The required proof must avoid full covariance inversion, handle row-dependent positive-semidefinite limits over the whole-array class \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\), and control the discontinuous selector by its one-dimensional positive variance margin. The reported decimal is reproducible quadrature of the exact formula; strict undercoverage follows from the analytic sign theorem rather than a certified numerical error bound.
body.honest_scope: The theorem concerns exactly two predeclared square bridge systems, ridge penalty one, stationary geometrically beta-mixing panels, fixed moment and rank radii, and positive ATT and selector-contrast variance margins. The split-sample variance margin is not separately assumed: \(V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}\geq V_s\geq\nu\) follows from its definition. The conventional interval uses the full pre-period sample for both selection and bridge fitting and uses its own fitted-score Bartlett standard error with bandwidth \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\); it is distinct from the early-select, gap-separated correction. The open correction is posed for each fixed finite \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}\) over whole arrays in \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\), not over unrelated per-row laws. The analysis does not cover the actual rectangular, simplex-constrained six-donor and ten-proxy rule used in the published West-German application, estimate the local population loss drift, recover full-pre-period efficiency after splitting, or solve the three-or-more-role cone problem. The exact-tie symmetry mechanism, generic sample splitting, and Bartlett HAC are established ingredients. The new claim is their proximal selected-coordinate coverage frontier and primitive realization. Under a fixed role or a diverging loss gap, the construction reduces to published fixed-role proximal normality; this is a sanity reduction, not a contribution.
